Throughout the Edo period, as one of the three principal shrines of the Akita Domain, it held a shrine estate of 30 koku.

Originally, {{ill|Yamamoto District, Akita|ceb|Yamamoto-gun|fr|District de Yamamoto|id|Distrik Yamamoto, Akita|it|Distretto di Yamamoto|ja|山本郡|kk|Ямамото (уезд)|ko|야마모토군|pl|Powiat Yamamoto (Akita)|ru|Ямамото (уезд)|th|อำเภอยามาโมโตะ|uk|Повіт Ямамото|zh|山本郡|qid=Q1155896}} referred to what is now {{ill|Senboku District, Akita|ceb|Semboku-gun|fr|District de Senboku (Akita)|id|Distrik Senboku, Akita|it|Distretto di Senboku (Akita)|ja|仙北郡|kk|Сембоку (уезд, Акита)|ko|센보쿠군 (아키타현)|pl|Powiat Senboku|ru|Сембоку (уезд, Акита)|uk|Повіт Сембоку (Акіта)|zh|仙北郡|qid=Q733727}}. Plates excavated from the {{ill|Hotta-no-saku|ja|払田柵跡|qid=Q11497278}} also bear the inscription “Yamamoto.” There is a theory that, in order to identify the Shikinaisha “Yamamoto District, one-seat small Soegawa Shrine” with the present Soegawa Shrine, an area formerly called “Hiyama District” was renamed “Yamamoto District.”

Originally, {{ill|Mount Takaoka|ja|高岳山 (秋田県)|qid=Q17225894|lt=Mount Takaoka}} had a shrine called Kōmine Shrine, whose enshrined deity was {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993}}. According to records, when the Kubota Domain was asked by the Yoshida family of Kyoto in {{ill|1714|ab|1714|af|1714|als|1714|am|1714 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1714|ar|1714|ary|1714|arz|1714|ast|1714|avk|1714|az|1714|azb|۱۷۱۴ (میلادی)|ba|1714 йыл|ban|1714|bar|1714|bcl|1714|be|1714|be_x_old|1714|bg|1714|bn|১৭১৪|bo|༡༧༡༤ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭১৪|br|1714|bs|1714.|ca|1714|cdo|1714 nièng|ce|1714 шо|ceb|1714|ckb|١٧١٤|co|1714|crh|1714|cs|1714|csb|1714|cv|1714|cy|1714|da|1714|de|1714|diq|1714|el|1714|eml|1714|eo|1714|es|1714|et|1714|eu|1714|fa|۱۷۱۴ (میلادی)|fi|1714|fo|1714|fr|1714|frp|1714|frr|1714|fur|1714|fy|1714|ga|1714|gan|1714年|gcr|1714|gd|1714|gl|1714|gv|1714|he|1714|hi|१७१४|hr|1714.|hsb|1714|ht|1714 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1714|hy|1714|hyw|1714 թուական|ia|1714|id|1714|ilo|1714|io|1714|is|1714|it|1714|ja|1714年|jv|1714|ka|1714|kaa|1714|kk|1714 жыл|kn|೧೭೧೪|ko|1714년|krc|1714 джыл|la|1714|lb|1714|lez|1714 йис|li|1714|lij|1714|lmo|1714|lt|1714 m.|lv|1714. gads|mai|१७१४|map_bms|1714|mdf|1714|mg|1714|mhr|1714|mi|1714|min|1714|mk|1714|mr|इ.स. १७१४|mrj|1714 и|ms|1714|my|၁၇၁၄|myv|1714 ие|mzn|۱۷۱۴|nah|1714|nap|1714|nds|1714|new|सन् १७१४|nl|1714|nn|1714|no|1714|nrm|1714|nso|1714|oc|1714|olo|1714|or|୧୭୧୪|os|1714-æм аз|pl|1714|pnb|1714|pt|1714|qu|1714|ro|1714|ru|1714 год|rue|1714|sa|१७१४|sah|1714|scn|1714|sd|1714ع|se|1714|sh|1714.|shn|1714|simple|1714|sk|1714|sl|1714|smn|1714|sq|1714|sr|1714|su|1714|sv|1714|sw|1714|szl|1714|ta|1714|te|1714|tg|Соли 1714|th|พ.ศ. 2257|tk|1714|tl|1714|tly|1714|tr|1714|tt|1714 ел|uk|1714|ur|1714ء|uz|1714|vec|1714|vi|1714|vls|1714|wa|1714|war|1714|wuu|1714年|xmf|1714|yi|1714|zh|1714年|zh_min_nan|1714 nî|zh_yue|1714年|qid=Q6878}} about the existence of Soegawa Shrine, the domain’s shrine magistrate, Mogi Tomonori, regarded Mount Takaoka as a sacred site and established Soegawa Shrine by jointly enshrining Kōmine Shrine. Local elders say, “This place is called Hatarazawa and also Horoha-yama; though one mountain, it has eight valleys.” The *Gun’yūki* records, “It may be the main sanctuary of Mount Horoha.” Soegawa is also read as “Soikawa.”<ref>*The Gods and Shrines of Akita*, by Hisaji Satō, Akita Shinshū Research Association, 1981</ref>

[[File:Takaokayama Zyoyatô.JPG|thumb|right|Mount Takaoka – Soegawa Shrine stone lantern]]
The stone lantern at the third torii gate on the mountainside (commonly called the middle torii) was a permanent lantern approximately 2.5 meters tall. In the past, it served as a lighthouse for boats traveling across Hachirōgata Lagoon.

== Northernmost Shikinaisha ==
In terms of its present location, it is the northernmost Shikinaisha in Japan. However, according to shrine tradition based on the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}, the original site of Soegawa Shrine was the present {{ill|Dake Rokusho Shrine|ja|嶽六所神社|qid=Q11477429}}. As this view is supported by {{ill|Kogakkan University|de|Kōgakkan-Universität|fa|دانشگاه کوگاکان|id|Universitas Kogakkan|ja|皇學館大学|tt|Когаккан университеты|zh|皇学馆大学|qid=Q1797584}} and many local historians, the shrine that should be considered the northernmost in its original location is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiga Riwake Shrine}} in {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Iwate|af|Iwate-prefektuur|an|Prefectura d'Iwate|ar|إيواته (محافظة)|az|İvate prefekturası|azb|ایواته اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Iwaté|bcl|Prepekturang Iwate|be|Іватэ (прэфектура)|bg|Ивате
